- Output: A set of wavelet coefficients $C$ organized in a hierarchical structure (pyramid), consisting of one approximation subband and multiple detail subbands (horizontal, vertical, depth, and combinations thereof) at each decomposition level.
The output is typically stored as a set of 3D arrays.
- Approximation subband $A$: Size $\lceil N/2 \rceil \times \lceil N/2 \rceil \times \lceil N/2 \rceil$.
- Detail subbands: Seven subbands of the same size as $A$, representing high-frequency components along different axes (e.g., $D_{xxx}, D_{xxy}, \dots$).
**Pass 1 (X-axis):** Apply the 1D DWT to every row (along the X-axis) of the volume.
This splits the volume into low-pass (approximation) and high-pass (detail) components along X.
**Pass 2 (Y-axis):** Apply the 1D DWT to every column (along the Y-axis) of the results from Pass 1.
**Pass 3 (Z-axis):** Apply the 1D DWT to every depth line (along the Z-axis) of the results from Pass 2.
This process generates the subbands for one level.
Let $h$ be the low-pass filter coefficients and $g$ be the high-pass filter coefficients.

In 3D, the approximation coefficient $A[i,j,k]$ at level $L$ is computed by convolving the input with the tensor product of the low-pass filters $h_x \otimes h_y \otimes h_z$ followed by downsampling by 2 in each dimension.
The detail coefficients are computed similarly using combinations of $h$ and $g$ (e.g., $g_x \otimes h_y \otimes h_z$ for the horizontal detail band).

- Dimensionality: The algorithm assumes the volume dimensions are divisible by $2^L$ for $L$ levels, or requires padding to handle non-power-of-two dimensions.
For lossless requirements, see [3D Integer Wavelet Transform](6956-3d-integer-wavelet-transform.md).
- **Time Complexity:** $O(N^3)$ for a volume of size $N^3$, as each voxel is processed a constant number of times per level.
Recursive decomposition adds a logarithmic factor in depth.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(N^3)$ for the input and output coefficients.
The hierarchical structure requires storing all subbands.
- **When to use:** General-purpose volume compression where axis-aligned features are dominant or when a simple baseline is needed.

- **When not to use:** When lossless integer arithmetic is required (use [3D Integer Wavelet Transform](6956-3d-integer-wavelet-transform.md)), or when data has strong non-axis-aligned structures (use [Directional Adaptive Discrete Wavelet Transform](7554-directional-adaptive-discrete-wavelet-transform.md)).
